title: Only 12% Pass This Chef's Entrance Exam
summary: Explore Kitchen Induction, Prep Bench, Kitchen Craft, Kitchen Gauntlet, Chef’s Table across five six-question rounds.

landing.intro:
Read the clues. Make the connections.
Put your thinking to the test.

about.body:
Five rounds offer different angles on this challenge: Kitchen Induction, Prep Bench, Kitchen Craft, Kitchen Gauntlet, Chef’s Table. Each round contains six distinct questions.

Choose one of four answers and move on automatically. There is no time limit. A short rewarded ad opens the quiz, each next round and the final result. The target is 24 correct answers out of 30. The result describes this quiz attempt only.

For entertainment and general learning only. This quiz is not a culinary qualification, professional kitchen assessment or food-safety certification. Always follow local food-safety requirements and qualified guidance.

steps: Press Start, watch a short rewarded ad and begin.
Choose one answer per question and progress through five rounds.
Complete all 30 questions to reveal your result. You can then unlock the full breakdown.

chef-r1q1.question: Which tool is best for gripping and turning hot food in a pan?

chef-r1q2.question: A sauce tastes rich and heavy but lacks brightness. Which small addition is most likely to rebalance it?

chef-r1q3.question: Which method cooks food in vapour above simmering water?

chef-r1q4.question: Which ingredient produces gas that helps a yeast dough rise?

chef-r1q5.question: A recipe uses 300 g of flour per batch. How much is needed for two batches?

chef-r1q6.question: Raw poultry was prepared on a board. Salad needs preparing next. What is safest?

answers.a1: Wipe the used board, then prepare salad on it
answers.a2: Turn the board over and use the clean-looking side
answers.a3: Rinse the board quickly with cold water
answers.a4: Use a cleaned and sanitised board and work surface

chef-r2q2.question: Which tool is designed to combine a liquid dressing smoothly?

chef-r2q5.question: A recipe says to add chopped parsley after the finished sauce comes off the heat. What is the most likely purpose?

chef-r3q2.question: What does a gentle simmer usually look like?

chef-r5q3.question: A muffin recipe using wheat flour says to mix only until no dry flour remains. Why stop at that point?

answers.a1: To avoid losing all the raising agent
answers.a2: Extra mixing can make the crumb tougher
answers.a3: To keep melted fat from separating
answers.a4: To stop the tops browning too early

chef-r5q6.question: A tray enters a preheated 180°C oven at 14:10 for 25 minutes. When should it first be checked?

chef-r2q6.question: A glass jar breaks beside uncovered prepared food. What should happen?

answers.a1: Remove visible glass and keep the food
answers.a2: Move the food away and continue service
answers.a3: Discard exposed food and clean the area safely
answers.a4: Cover the food and clean after service

chef-r2q3.question: Why cut potatoes into similar-sized pieces before roasting?

answers.a1: So they absorb exactly the same amount of oil
answers.a3: So the oven temperature cannot change
answers.a4: So they cook at a similar rate

chef-r4q2.question: A reduced sauce is too salty; unsalted stock is available and its consistency can be adjusted. What is the best correction?

answers.a3: Add unsalted stock gradually and retaste

chef-r3q1.question: Vegetables in a crowded hot pan turn pale and wet. What best explains it?

answers.a1: Released moisture was trapped, so the vegetables steamed
answers.a2: The pan was too hot and sealed the moisture inside
answers.a3: The vegetables absorbed the oil before they could brown
answers.a4: Turning them too often created the extra moisture

chef-r5q2.question: Why are cold pieces of butter kept distinct in a flaky pastry dough?

answers.a1: Distinct butter pieces make the dough rise before baking
answers.a2: Distinct butter pieces melt and help separate flaky layers
answers.a3: Distinct butter pieces stop the flour absorbing any water
answers.a4: Distinct butter pieces prevent the pastry from browning

chef-r6q1.question: A recipe uses 300 g rice for 4 portions. How much is needed for 10 portions?

chef-r6q6.question: A cook develops vomiting during service. What is the responsible first decision?

answers.a1: Finish the current task, then report it
answers.a2: Stop handling food and report it promptly
answers.a3: Put on fresh gloves and continue

chef-r8q1.question: Which tool is designed to sift dry flour to remove lumps?

chef-r8q3.question: Which method uses dry oven heat?

chef-r8q5.question: Three portions each weigh 175 g. What is the total?

chef-r8q6.question: A serving plate is chipped at the rim just before service. What should happen?

answers.a2: Use it only for cold food

chef-r10q1.question: Onion cooks first and fresh herbs finish the dish, but both were prepared in one bowl. What setup change follows the recipe?

answers.a1: Prepare them separately for when each is added
answers.a3: Add the herbs at the start

chef-r10q2.question: A dish tastes rich and heavy but needs freshness. Which finishing adjustment best balances it?

chef-r10q3.question: A dish is browning quickly outside but remains below its centre target; a lower-oven finish is allowed. What is the best next step?

answers.a4: Lower the heat and continue until the stated target is reached

chef-r10q4.question: A biscuit recipe specifies 200 g flour and 100 g butter; 200 g of each was used. Why did the biscuits spread?

chef-r10q5.question: An order increases from 12 to 18 portions at 150 g each. What total prepared mass is required?

chef-r10q6.question: Rice sat warm through service with unverified time and temperature; a fresh verified batch is available. What is safest?

answers.a1: Reheat the old rice and serve it
answers.a2: Use the fresh batch and isolate the old rice
answers.a3: Mix the old rice into the fresh batch
answers.a4: Serve the old rice because it is warm
